start.speaker: narrator
text: Ketelsteeg, Tuesday. The rain has stopped for a moment and left the tram rails shining.

You have been in Steenbeek for four days. You came for the room, which is cheap because it is an attic over a shuttered stationer's, and the job, which starts on Monday. The boxes are still stacked against the wall.

The previous tenant left something behind. It is a slab of wood, about the size of a tea tray, with a grid of lines cut into the top -- nineteen one way, nineteen the other. Beside it sits a wooden bowl of small flat stones, black and white, cool to the touch.
You have turned the whole arrangement over twice looking for instructions. There are none.
It is too deliberate to be a chopping board and too heavy to be a game.

resolve.speaker: narrator
text: Somebody in a town this size will know what it is.
You put the bowl in the crook of your arm, tuck the board under it, and go out.
